items.title: Fail-safe behaviour when the Mediator is slow — architecture (owner L425 item 0e: "review and provide the answers and guards; … might allow the user to decide in some cases depending on context and who we are talking to; definitely not a global give-up-and-send")
items.state_text: done as a design (2026-10-24, Fable FS-1): ADR-0023 **Proposed** — §2 measured: dev real inference commit → verdict p50 / p95 / max 1.27 / 1.72 / 2.23 s (10.4 % over 1.5 s, 0 / 300 over 3 s), mock dev 0.95 / 1.22 s (round-trip floor), **staging in region send → checked p50 0.44 / p95 0.79 s on real messages (CT-10 smoke), 0.12 / 0.18 s tier 0, 0 unchecked of 300**; ≈ 2–5 % of in-region messages pass 1 s, < 1 % pass 1.5 s; an outage makes it 100 %; provider quota ≈ 15 k guard calls a day is the rate ceiling. Decision: **no silent automatic release by default** (`fail_safe.slow.auto_release = never`, selectable per market with the predicted share shown, high-impact); one "Still checking" state (glyph `checking`) at `slow.ask_after_ms` (1 500 ms production, 3 000 dev) for every mediated message; **the sender may release their own message unchecked only in a 1:1 with a known contact**, tier 0 clean, reader allows, ≤ 30 / h, always marked, late block kept, verdict wins a race; the reader's standing preference (`contacts_now` default; minors forced `wait`); groups and strangers wait; fail-closed unchanged; telemetry + console predictor. Owner questions: **Q1** sender release at all and in which company (recommend yes, bounded), **Q2** automatic release to contacts during outages (recommend keep the option, start `never`). Lead: accept the ADR, apply §10, close item 0e, add Q1 / Q2 to the decisions page

items.title: C: `gateway.test.ts` › "mediated (stub Mediator PASS)" got the message released unchecked (no `outcome`) for both WS impls once in the 33-minute full Railway run; passes alone and after conformance-live — give the test a fail-open timeout above the stub Mediator's worst latency on the shared stack, or a fail-closed conversation, so load cannot turn it into an unchecked release
items.state_text: done (wave 12 C, 2026-10-20): **verdict: the fail-open timeout under load, not an ordering gap.** On the Railway stack the stub-Mediator round trip is already ≈ 1.0–1.5 s without load (baseline 1386–2038 ms after accept, one of three unchecked) against the 1.5 s window; reproduced deterministically under load (event-loop stall + 24-message burst + slow Mediator outcomes): every fail-open message released unchecked was released after its `deadline_at` and logged (`mediation.released{via: timeout, code: timer}`), while every fail-closed message under the same load was released only with the signed PASS (0/12 unchecked, no timer, no refusal); forced fail-closed timer rows and forged `deliver_unchecked` notices never release. Latency (40 sequential messages, no load, laptop → Railway): send→ack p50 1132 / p95 1220 ms (the accept transaction; `deadline_at` starts inside it), ack → Mediator outcome at the dispatcher p50 330 / p95 362 / max 691 ms (relay + Mediator + result stream), outcome → recipient p50 1127 / p95 1207 ms, accept → release p50 1062 / p95 1097 / max 1494 ms of the 1500 ms window: the margin goes to the server's serial statements at ≈ 70 ms RTT, not to the Mediator (P1-C-10-F6-F3). G wave 6's unchecked releases were logged by the dispatcher (`mediation.outcome fail_open`, the registered form of `mediation.released{via: timeout}`). Recommendation: `fail_safe.fail_open_timeout_ms` = 3000 on the dev and staging layers (the guardrail maximum; what conformance already uses) until staging measures the distribution; production stays 1.5 s pending real inference latencies (P1-D-01-F4). Hardening: deadlines compared on the database clock (`dueTimers`), the Mediator's `failsafe.timeout` notice applied only once `deadline_at` passed (`dueOnly`), unchecked releases of fail-closed records refused in `onDeadline` and the store; `gateway.test.ts` accepts a timeout only as a logged release after the deadline (20/20). Tests `apps/server/test/integration/wave12-failsafe-load.test.ts` (4), docs `docs/mechanisms/gated-release.md`; evidence `docs/testing/walkthroughs/P1-C-w12.md`; follow-ups P1-C-10-F6-F1, P1-C-10-F6-F2

Triage whether the sealed sheet's `sendAnywayAllowed` / `actions.anyway` or the client's gate drops it; `held.spec` runs the flow once offered
items.state_text: done (wave 45 H, 2026-10-23: D part wave 12 D; the client gate fixed in P1-G-w6-F5-F1 (wave 11 E1); G part done (wave 7 G: send anyway green on Chromium and WebKit)) · was: D part done (wave 12 D, 2026-10-20): the Mediator is correct — for G's case (Standard, first contact from a stranger, controversial harassment + profanity label as the HTTP mock answers) the decision has `send_anyway_allowed: true` and the sealed sheet `sendAnywayAllowed: true` with `NudgeAction.ANYWAY` (`packages/mediation/test/pipeline.test.ts` "P1-G-w6-F5"). Likely cause on the client (E1): `ServicesProvider` computes `sendAnyway` once inside its `useMemo` from `engine.heldActionsSupported`, which reads the ServerHello features — before the hello arrives it is false and the memo never recomputes, so the sheet gets `anywaySupported=false` (clarity answers read `engine.clarityAnswersSupported` at render time and work). Fix suggestion: always pass a `sendAnyway` function and gate on `engine?.heldActionsSupported` at render time → P1-G-w6-F5-F1 (E1); G part **done** (wave 7 G): `held.spec` send anyway green on Chromium and WebKit (E1 wave 11 un-skipped it)

Likely cause on the client (E1): `ServicesProvider` computes `sendAnyway` once inside its `useMemo` from `engine.heldActionsSupported`, which reads the ServerHello features — before the hello arrives it is false and the memo never recomputes, so the sheet gets `anywaySupported=false` (clarity answers read `engine.clarityAnswersSupported` at render time and work). Fix suggestion: always pass a `sendAnyway` function and gate on `engine?.heldActionsSupported` at render time → P1-G-w6-F5-F1 (E1); G part **done** (wave 7 G): `held.spec` send anyway green on Chromium and WebKit (E1 wave 11 un-skipped it)

items.title: C: a group proposer leaving or removed expires their open proposal in a **separate** transaction after the membership one (`GroupService.membersLeft` → `expireForLeavers`; a failure is only logged), and accept does not re-check that the proposer is still a member, so after a failed expiry an admin can accept a departed member's proposal (consents naming a non-member) until its `expires_at`. Either expire it inside the membership transaction (the entry at the seq right after the `MembershipChange`), or treat an open proposal whose proposer is no longer a member as expired on every list, propose and answer, as `expireDueIn` does for a due one; test: a failing expiry hook, then the accept → 409 `scope.proposal_closed` (`expired`). Live `scope.group-leave` already pins the order (EXPIRED after the membership entry)
items.state_text: done (wave 21 C, 2026-10-22): the second option — `expireDueIn` (every list, propose and answer) also expires an open proposal whose proposer is no longer a member (`expireOne(…, 'left')`, which itself re-checks the membership in its transaction, so a proposer added back keeps it open), and the accept transaction re-checks the proposer's membership (409 `scope.proposal_closed`, `state: expired`). Integration `wave20-scope.test.ts` › "a departed proposer’s proposal cannot be accepted": the leaver hook fails once (spy), the row stays `proposed`, the admin's accept → 409 `scope.proposal_closed` `expired`, listed expired, policy version unchanged, the EXPIRED entry has no actor; without the fix the same test gets 200 `accepted` (run against the previous service). Live conformance 49 / 49 after the change. `docs/mechanisms/scope.md`

items.title: D (gateway owner): does `rephrase` get the group's topic as an input?
items.state_text: done (wave 30 D, 2026-10-22): **decided no**, no gateway schema, prompt or registry change. Reasons (`docs/mechanisms/scope.md` §Built in wave 30 D): (1) the suggestions rewrite tone in the sender's own meaning — an off-topic message cannot be made on topic without changing what the sender says, which the rephrase rule forbids; the answers there are "send as is" / edit and later the split (owner item 0ba (5)); (2) a topic line pulls its own words into suggestions and Coach's `ADDS_FACTS` backstop sees only numbers, days, dates, times and amounts, not topic nouns or purposes; (3) the topic is admin-typed free text: in `classify` it moves one score, in `rephrase` it would shape words every member can send with one tap. Revisit with the split task (needs the topic and a subset-fidelity check)

items.title: D / lead: a failover for the Assistant planner. The router ranks latency fit before the registry order, so a fast tool-calling model placed second in `assistant` (Mistral Small 3.2, p95 1.26 s inside the 1.5 s `sync` target) would lead while gpt-oss-120b (registry p95 3.97 s) does not fit: either a gateway option that keeps an alias in registry order (e.g. ranking `fixed`, or a per-candidate `failover_only`; contract change, lead) or the lead's decision to make a faster model the planner (whisper and public probes on it); then a clean paced quality run of the candidate (≥ 5 s between records at ≈ 7.9 k tokens a call against 100 k tokens a minute, ≈ 0.065 USD for 47 records) under the wave 33 D rule (R2–R4)
items.state_text: done (wave 45 H, 2026-10-23: decided (L293) and done (wave 35 D) as the row's own cell says) · was: decided (lead, 2026-10-22, L293): the router's rule (a candidate that fits the latency target ranks before registry order) is right for routing and stays; a backup that must stay second needs an explicit `failover_only` flag on the registry entry (additive gateway option, CT-05, D 35 proposes the schema), then the clean paced quality run under the same pre-registered rule. **done (wave 35 D, 2026-10-22):** (1) registry candidate field `failover_only` (optional; schema regenerated): never ranked ahead of a candidate of its pool that lacks the flag and is not open (latency fit, cost, registry and policy order still order the rest); leads only while the primary is open, filtered out, killed (`next_candidate` drops the real primary) or on a pin; never a canary (validation) or the sticky choice; an alias needs one candidate without it; the wave 33 R5 unit test now shows the flagged Mistral entry second; no routed candidate changes. (2) clean paced run (6 s pace, rule committed `60388b4e` before any call): 47 / 47 answered, 0 rate-limited; R1 pass, **R2 fail (strict tool hit 0.77 < 0.95**; misses: `destructive` 5 / 10, `public_answer` 3 / 10, `named` 2 / 6, `ambiguous` 1 / 5; ar 0.57, es 0.56), R3 pass (0 / 0), R4 pass (p95 1 433 ms), R5 pass (flagged, ranked second) → **not added**, registry stays `alpha-2026-10-22.6`; 0.0648 USD; quota Mistral 3 807 881 → 3 438 163. Evidence [`P1-D-w35.md`](testing/walkthroughs/P1-D-w35.md), [`2026-10-22-wave35-planner-failover`](testing/evals/2026-10-22-wave35-planner-failover/README.md); docs `docs/api/model-registry.md`, `docs/mechanisms/assistant.md`, `docs/11-ai-architecture.md`, gateway README. items.title: C: receipts are applied one reader at a time per gateway (`ReceiptBatcher.flush` → `ReceiptService.apply` per user, one transaction per conversation, ≈ 10–11 round trips each), so receipt lag grows with the readers that have marks pending (≈ 0.77 s each on dev) and a large group's readers block every other conversation's receipts (LT-03 at 256: 405 serial transactions over 264 s; a 1:1 run's receipts 174 s late). items.title: C 28: (a) `proposeLevel`'s order — the idempotency lookup first (a retry after an accept or a version change still answers 200 with the item), keyed on conversation and proposer (the same id from the other person or in another conversation is 409 `level.proposal_id_reused`, never their proposal); then `level.not_one_to_one`; for Off: 422 `level.not_offered` where Off is not offered, 422 `policy.locked` under the minors' lock, `level.off_direct` only where Off can be set alone; then `policy.version_changed`, `level.not_offered`, `level.no_change`. items.title: C: `apps/server/test/integration/wave28c-levels.test.ts:479-540` (`race`) cannot tell the under-lock refusal from a pre-read refusal — the codes it asserts are the ones the pre-reads answer when a request arrives after the winner's commit (the accept: `expireDueIn` then `closed(r0.state)`, `modules/scope/level-proposals.ts:421-433` → 409 `level.proposal_closed` `expired`; the Off write: `st0.version`, `modules/scope/service.ts:761-765` → 409 `policy.version_changed`), and `won` is derived (`:510`), never asserted per order, so with the fixed 300 ms + 1 500 ms sleeps (`:496, :500, :504`) on the remote dev stack the test passes even when the second request never reached the lock. Fix: before `COMMIT` the holder polls `pg_stat_activity` until two other backends of this database are in `wait_event_type = 'Lock'` (time-out = fail), then `expect(won).toBe(first)` (row-lock waiters are granted in queue order) — each order is then really exercised and the loser provably refused by the re-check under the lock (`level-proposals.ts:514-521`, `service.ts:843-847`)

items.title: C: the `FOR UPDATE OF conversations` fix (`25cef141`: `service.ts:397-411` locks the row alone, `:437` reads the join as a second statement) is right, and every locked caller reads the policy through it after the lock (`service.ts:843, 1068, 1167, 1251, 1329, 1421`; `level-proposals.ts:367, 451, 511, 605`; no path reads the policy under the lock before taking it; the pre-reads on `deps.db` are re-validated under the lock by version, or by proposal state and level) — but it holds only because the second statement gets a fresh snapshot in READ COMMITTED (nothing in `apps/server` sets an isolation level today). Under REPEATABLE READ, or folded into one statement (a `WITH … FOR UPDATE` CTE joined to `policies`), the joined read returns the **old** policy row, the version re-check passes wrongly and the loser overwrites the winner. Fix: say so in `state()`'s comment, keep the lock and the joined read two statements when P1-C-w28-F1–F4 fold the round trips, and a unit test that the write path's transactions set no isolation level

items.title: Lead (+ F, B): three consequences of the limit as decided (L311: any SUPERSEDED / WITHDRAWN counts until `expires_at`; absent = 2, TTL 168 h) — (a) the **other person's counter-proposal** supersedes the proposer's open proposal and that SUPERSEDED row counts against the *proposer* for 7 days, so an answer-by-counter costs the first proposer a slot (the intent names the proposer's own supersede); consider counting a SUPERSEDED row only when `superseded_by` names the same proposer; (b) under `ttl_hours = 0` a superseded or withdrawn proposal counts for ever, so two withdrawals lock the proposer out of that conversation until the other person accepts or declines — nothing of theirs is open to answer; consider refusing `ttl_hours = 0` with a limit in F's schema or expiring the count after the default TTL; (c) a live run against a **persistent** fixture (not the server's fresh-database live test) can repeat `scope.proposal` / `level.proposal` at most twice per TTL window per fixture user (each run leaves one superseded proposal per person), so a persistent-fixture runner needs fresh users per run

items.title: C: `wave28c-levels.test.ts`'s race on the dev stack — the first request provably waits on the conversation row lock (the holder polls `pg_stat_activity`, time-out = fail) and the first-issued request wins in both orders, but the **second** request did not appear as a second lock waiter within 8–20 s in the Off-first order (both requests still in flight; `pg_stat_activity` showed only the outbox publisher and pollers), so its refusal may come from its pre-reads once the winner commits, not from the re-check under the lock. The test records `secondAtLock` and tolerates its absence; find where the second request waits (not in Postgres: a Node-side single flight — the policy service, the HTTP server — or undici's connection reuse) and make both requests reach the lock before the holder commits

items.title: C: `apps/server/src/modules/conversations/group-key.ts:202-204, 249-258` reads the caller's role, the stored state and the members' registered devices on `deps.db` and runs `groupKeyShareDecision` before the transaction; under the conversation row lock (`:283-291`) only the generation and the check are re-checked. Every membership change takes the same row lock in its own transaction, so one that commits between `:250` and `:283` is invisible to the decision: a member removed meanwhile keeps a wrap — `G'` sealed to a former member's device is logged (`:381-391`) and recorded as a recipient (`:351-363`), and only the reader's window (`modules/messages/reader.ts:45`) stands between that device and the key a reset on removal exists to deny it (key material, not access control, is the design's guarantee); a member added meanwhile gets no wrap and the reset passes without `recipients_incomplete`; a demoted admin's reset passes. Fix: under the lock re-read the caller's membership row and `members(tx, convId)` and re-run `groupKeyShareDecision` (its answers exist: 403 `groups.admin_required`, 422 `group_key.share_invalid` `recipient_not_member`, 422 `group_key.recipients_incomplete`), as the generation is re-checked; a race test as `wave28c-levels.test.ts` `race` (P1-B-w24-CR1's `pg_stat_activity` wait) with a removal and an add committing while the reset waits for the lock

items.title: C: the platform policy read before the lock is re-validated by the conversation's own versions only. `accept` (`modules/scope/level-proposals.ts:573, 599-602`) reuses `pre` while `policies.version` and `scope_layer_version` equal `st0`'s; the platform policy serial (global and market layers: `levels.offered`, the fail-mode rules) is not compared, so a layer published while the accept waits for the lock is missed, the target is checked against the older `levels.offered` and the older `serial` is stamped into the new `policies` row (`platformPolicyVersion`). The same holds for `setDirect` (`modules/scope/service.ts:821, 892-895`) and the reset with re-sealed rules (`group-key.ts:302, 364`), which re-check `policies.version` only. The read was never atomic with a platform publish (the snapshot is trusted for `serialTtlMs`, 1 s, `modules/policy/platform.ts:143, 218`), but it was at most that old when read under the lock; now it is that old plus the lock wait (the other writer's hold, 0.6-0.7 s in wave 34's trace, more under contention). Fix: keep the read before the lock and reuse it only if the lock was granted within `serialTtlMs` of it, else read again under the lock (the common case costs nothing; the stale case reads from the snapshot or one `policy_serial` row), one helper for the three writers, and a test that holds the lock past the TTL. Text: protocol.md §Level proposals said the policy is read under the lock - corrected in this wave to the pre-read with the version re-check (mechanisms/scope.md already said so)

items.title: C / B: a linked (or restored) device cannot verify the epoch-key grants of its hand-off or backup on the real server: `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/keys` serves only bundles carrying a wrap for the **calling** device, so `acceptEpochKeyGrant` has no stored bundle to check against and the new device reads no history under earlier epochs (D of `P1-E1-w32`: 5 epoch keys handed over, 0 accepted). items.title: C: serve `GET /v1/conversations/{convId}/epoch-bundles` (`docs/api/protocol.md` §Epoch bundles for the user's devices). (1) **Migration** (next free number; with a down file): `epoch_recipients(conv_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES conversations ON DELETE CASCADE, epoch integer NOT NULL, user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users ON DELETE CASCADE, PRIMARY KEY (conv_id, epoch, user_id))` — deliberately **no** reference to `devices` (revoked rows are purged at `retention_limits.metadata` and cascade `device_key_wraps`); backfill `INSERT INTO epoch_recipients (conv_id, epoch, user_id) SELECT DISTINCT w.conv_id, w.epoch, d.user_id FROM device_key_wraps w JOIN devices d ON d.id = w.device_id ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (epochs whose devices were already purged are lost; dev data only — count them in the PR). (2) **Write:** `KeysService.storeEpoch` inserts one row per distinct user of the validated device wraps (`validateEpoch`'s device rows already carry `userId`), in the same transaction wherever `storeEpoch` runs (`rotateConversationKeys`; any create path that stores keys). (3) **Read** `listEpochBundles(auth, convId, {sinceEpoch = 0, limit = 64})`: `assertMember` (current member, else 404 `conversation.not_found`), `limit` 1–256 and `sinceEpoch` ≥ 0 (else 400 `request.invalid`), then `SELECT k.epoch, k.bundle, k.created_at, k.created_by_device, k.mediator_key_id FROM conversation_keys k JOIN epoch_recipients r ON r.conv_id = k.conv_id AND r.epoch = k.epoch AND r.user_id = $caller_user WHERE k.conv_id = $conv AND k.epoch >= $since AND k.bundle IS NOT NULL ORDER BY k.epoch LIMIT $limit + 1`; serve the stored bytes unchanged; stop before the item that would pass 4 MiB of bundle bytes (always at least one) or at `limit`, and set `nextEpoch` to the first epoch not served (`EPOCH_BUNDLES_PAGE` in `@lucid/protocol`). `getConversationKeys` is unchanged. (4) **Client API draft.23:** `listEpochBundles` (tag conversations; query `sinceEpoch`, `limit`), response `EpochBundleList {items: [{epoch, bundle (Base64Url), createdAt, creatorDeviceId (Uuid), mediatorKeyId?}] (all but mediatorKeyId required), nextEpoch?}`, 400 / 401 / 404; regenerate the server's types (E1 regenerates the app's). (5) **Advertise** `SERVER_FEATURE_EPOCH_BUNDLES` (27) only while the migration is applied (as 23–25). (6) **Integration tests** (Railway stack; `apps/server/test/integration/`): a device linked after an epoch gets it here and not from `getConversationKeys`, bytes equal to the posted bundle; a removed member 404, and after it is added back never the epoch it missed (but its earlier ones); an epoch wrapped only to a device that was later revoked **and deleted by the retention purge** still listed for its user's new device; legacy epochs without a bundle never; another user's / conversation's epochs never; paging by `limit` and by the 4 MiB cap with `nextEpoch`; `migrations.test.ts` chain and table expectations (rule 15). (7) **Live fixture:** `conversations.history` in `conformance-live.test.ts` — a new group (a owner, b member, Standard fail-open with the stub key, or Off; no other check uses it) `{convId, level, failMode: 'open', epoch: 1, mediatorKeyId}`; `total` 52 → 53. **At the merge of wave 30 B (before C ships):** the runner has 53 checks and `keys.linked-history` skips ("server does not advertise EPOCH_BUNDLES"), which the skip-free guard (P1-G-w21-F1) rejects — the lead raises `total` to 53 and lets exactly that skip through with its reason in the same merge (two lines in `conformance-live.test.ts`), or merges wave 30 B together with C's half. Docs: `docs/mechanisms/keys-and-wraps.md` (the recipients table, the read), `docs/api/openapi-client.md`, data model

items.title: F: `e2e/wave37.spec.ts:34` ("open drafts wrap a long reason; the filter field fits the longest key path") fails on WebKit desktop, LTR and RTL, deterministically (`field.overflow` 19, expected ≤ 1; Chromium passes): the filter field is wider than its row in WebKit. The nightly WebKit shard 1 will be red on it until fixed
items.state_text: done (wave 46 F, 2026-10-24): root cause — WebKit resolves `ui-monospace` to SF Mono (0.618 em per glyph) while Chromium does not support `ui-monospace` and falls back to Menlo (0.602 em; measured in both engines); the field was sized in a fixed 0.6 em of the page's 14 px and capped at its 712 px row, so the 81-character longest path needed 701 px of the 684 px text box in WebKit (scrollWidth 731 vs clientWidth 712: the 19 px), and passed in Chromium by 1.3 px. Fix (`apps/admin/src/styles/app.css` `.input.path-filter`): the field is always in the list's monospace face and size (`code.path`, 12 px) and sized `calc((var(--path-ch) + 2) * 1ch + 28px)` — each engine's own advance —, the placeholder keeps the script font (`::placeholder`, per script), so the width no longer changes when typing starts; the e2e assertions kept, plus the width empty = typed; `test/wave37.test.ts` (ch, no em factor, 12 px, placeholder fonts). `wave37.spec.ts` passes on WebKit and Chromium desktop LTR light and RTL dark and phone RTL dark (6 / 6, own port, one project per run); README · was: todo — follow-up ENV-GITHUB-F18-F1 (wave 47 H, 2026-10-24: no change to the filter field or `apps/admin/e2e/wave37.spec.ts` since wave 54 A (last touched 77ff0db3); the WebKit nightly shard stays red on it) · was: todo

items.state_text: not stated in docs/07a
